keyVerseText: He hath compassed the waters with bounds, until the day and night come to an end. until: Heb. until the end of light with darkness
rootMeaning: The root of חוּג (chûwg) is connected to the primitive root חָגַג (châgag), which carries the sense of moving in a circle, often in the context of celebration or a sacred procession. This root meaning highlights a physical and symbolic motion of encircling or circling around, which goes beyond the simple English gloss of "compass." It implies intentionality in drawing a boundary or making a complete circuit, evoking both spatial and ritual significance.
usageInScripture: The word חוּג (chûwg) appears only once in Scripture, translated as "He hath compassed" in Job 26:10. This singular usage emphasizes the act of encircling or encompassing, particularly in relation to God's control over creation. The consistent translation as "compassed" reveals the word's focus on surrounding or setting boundaries, highlighting God's sovereign ordering of the natural world.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding חוּג as an intentional act of encircling enriches our view of God's providence and sovereignty. It portrays God as one who not only creates but also defines and sustains order within creation by setting precise boundaries. This reflects the divine attribute of wisdom in governance and care, assuring believers of God's control over chaos and His faithful maintenance of the cosmos. Such imagery invites trust in God's comprehensive power and His purposeful design in all things.
keyVerseReflection: Job 26:10 states, "He hath compassed the waters with bounds, until the day and night come to an end," illustrating God's sovereign act of encircling the waters with limits. The use of חוּג here conveys God's authority in defining natural boundaries, preventing chaos from overwhelming creation. This word deepens the meaning of the verse by emphasizing God's deliberate and sustaining control over the universe's order, reinforcing His role as the ultimate Creator and Sustainer.
